correctness.rationale: Independent finite reconstruction from all 36 supplied facets gives 84/84 triangles and 90 present/36 missing four-simplices; on at most three vertices no nonzero 2-cycle can occur. The explicit ±1 integral 2-cocycle annihilates all 90 oriented tetrahedral boundaries, pairs ±1 (18 each) with the 36 missing tetrahedral sphere boundaries, and so certifies every missing support as a primitive nonzero class in published H2(K;Z)≅Z. Every present tetrahedron boundary is nullhomologous. Independent exhaustive 9! permutation check yields Aut size54 and missing support orbit sizes 9,27; pairing the cocycle after each relabelling shows H2 signs 27 positive, 27 negative. These exhaustive finite facts follow from complete facets, not partial sampling.
residual_risks: Integral rank-one homology is a published topological fact, not independently Smith-normal-form computed in this execution.

evidence: Classical descriptions establish the minimal triangulation, face-vector and symmetry. A known proper-induced-nonface collapse theorem (as recorded in assigned source comparisons) does not prove every tetrahedral sphere maps to a generator of H2(K;Z).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The topological triangulation and induced subcomplex results are broader background but do not visibly dominate inclusion-sensitive primitive carrier data.

evidence: Three-neighborliness plus H2=Z does NOT alone imply missing tetrahedral spheres are nonzero, still less primitive; the explicit cohomological functional with ±1 evaluations supplies a missing inclusion argument.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact cocycle is an independent witness for primitivity of all missing supports. Published automorphism order 54 is acknowledged as prior, so no incorrect new-group claim.

evidence: Every missing four-set carries a tetrahedral sphere pairing ±1 with an integral cohomology class; hence its class is primitive and nonzero. This is stronger than mere induced subcomplex homotopy equivalence.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Compared vertex-support systolic representatives of H2, missing-facet boundaries, induced tetrahedral spheres and action on H2. Simple-homotopy type alone does not determine inclusion-induced integral homology.

The old group size is acknowledged as background, and no generalization to other triangulations is claimed.
